nist_series_caveats.ref: NIST 4p->12s,13s f*n*^3 is ~25% below the smooth series defined by the published all-order values for n=5-10 (Safronova & Safronova, PRA 78, 052504 (2008), Table IV) and by NIST n<=11; the K 12s lifetime computed with them is 21% above the published SD value (1035 ns) while 7s-11s agree within 3%

NIST 4p->12s,13s f*n*^3 is ~25% below the smooth series defined by the published all-order values for n=5-10 (Safronova & Safronova, PRA 78, 052504 (2008), Table IV) and by NIST n<=11; the K 12s lifetime computed with them is 21% above the published SD value (1035 ns) while 7s-11s agree within 3%

NIST 4s->np f for n>=10 is 18-32% below the published central-potential values (Theodosiou, arXiv:2211.12664, Table IV: NIST/CET 1/2: 0.81, 0.76, 0.78, 0.83; 3/2: 0.74, 0.68, 0.70, 0.75 at n=10-13) while n<=8 agree within 8 %; the NIST/CET trend is the same as for 4p->ns n>=12
